Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown or velvety black velvety spots on leaves, causing premature yellowing and leaf drop. Scabby lesions also develop on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment_organic: Apply sulfur or copper-based sprays early in spring. Neem oil and Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicides can suppress early fungal spread.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment_chemical: Apply captan, myclobutanil, or mancozeb according to protective spray schedules during bud break and wet periods.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and compost or destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune tree canopies to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration. Plant scab-resistant cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with tan centers and purple margins. Cankers on bark, and dark, rotting fruit mummifying on the tree.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment_organic: Prune out dead wood and cankered branches 6-8 inches below infected tissue. Apply copper soap or lime sulfur.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment_chemical: Fungicides containing thiophanate-methyl, captan, or strobilurin-based formulations applied from silver tip through petal fall.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitize pruning tools between cuts. Remove mummified apples and brush piles from the orchard. Avoid mechanical trunk wounding.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish circular spots on upper leaf surfaces. Later, small tube-like fruiting structures appear on leaf undersides.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment_organic: Spray copper fungicides or sulfur as leaves emerge. Remove nearby Eastern Red Cedar trees if practical within 1-2 miles.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment_chemical: Apply sterol-inhibitor fungicides such as immunox (myclobutanil) or propiconazole every 7-10 days during the spring wet cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties (e.g., Liberty, Freedom, Enterprise). Inspect surrounding conifers and remove rust galls.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is vibrant green, firm, and free of discoloration, lesions, or curling. Tree shows vigorous seasonal growth.
Apple___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Maintain balanced compost mulch and soil organic matter.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue standard seasonal pruning, balanced fertilization (avoid excess nitrogen), and consistent drip watering.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Foliage exhibits deep emerald or forest green pigmentation with smooth margins and healthy new stem growth.
Blueberry___healthy.treatment_organic: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 - 5.5) using pine bark mulch and elemental sulfur.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Ensure well-drained acidic soil, adequate organic mulch, and regular drip irrigation avoid soaking leaves.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, talcum powder-like fungal patches on leaves and terminal shoots. Leaves may curl upward, distort, and drop prematurely.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment_organic: Spray potassium bicarbonate solution, wettable sulfur, or horticultural horticultural oils at 7-day intervals.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment_chemical: Apply triadimefon, myclobutanil, or triflumizole starting at petal fall through harvest according to label directions.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune interior branches to increase sunlight and wind penetration. Avoid high nitrogen fertilizer which triggers soft susceptible shoots.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are glossy, rich green, firm, and uniform without powdery residue, holes, or chlorosis.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment needed. Keep base mulched and watered during dry spells.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Annual pruning during dry weather to maintain open canopy structure.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Tan or grayish rectangular lesions restricted between leaf veins, leading to extensive leaf blight and premature plant death.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment_organic: Bio-fungicides containing Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens applied at early tasseling stage.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment_chemical: Fungicides with azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, or propiconazole applied at VT-R1 (tassel to silking) growth stage.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate crops with non-grasses (soybean, legumes) for at least 2 years. Plow residue under or adopt certified resistant hybrid seeds.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown to brick-red powdery pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment_organic: Neem-based botanical extracts or copper hydroxide sprays during early infection phases.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment_chemical: Apply pyraclostrobin, azoxystrobin, or tebuconazole if pustules appear before silking on susceptible hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids with Rp gene resistance. Plant early in the season to evade peak mid-summer airborne spore flights.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large, elongated cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches long) that coalesce, giving plants a frost-burned look.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment_organic: Apply copper sulfate or compost tea early in the season. Till infected crop residues deep into soil.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment_chemical: Use triazole or strobilurin fungicides (e.g., Headline AMP, Quilt Xcel) when lesion thresholds are exceeded before reproductive stages.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Utilize corn hybrids with Ht gene resistance. Practice crop rotation and reduce standing residue.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant green leaves with sturdy stems and no discoloration, lesions, or rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment_organic: Maintain good soil fertility with balanced N-P-K organic manures.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Practice rotational farming, ensure proper planting density, and keep weed competition minimal.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small circular reddish-brown leaf spots with black margins and black dots inside. Grapes turn into shriveled, hard, black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment_organic: Apply copper octanoate or lime sulfur spray prior to rain events during early shoot growth.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment_chemical: Apply mancozeb, captan, or kresoxim-methyl starting at 1-inch shoot growth through 4 weeks post-bloom.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out mummified berry clusters and dead canes during winter dormancy. Maximize canopy airflow.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf pattern with chlorotic and necrotic areas between green veins. Berries show tiny dark spots (measles).
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment_organic: Paint fresh pruning wounds with biocontrol agents such as Trichoderma. Prune in late winter during dry conditions.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment_chemical: Treat pruning cuts promptly with wound sealants or thiophanate-methyl pastes to prevent wound entry.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid pruning in wet weather. Mark and gently remove severely stunted or dead cordons and replace trunks gradually.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown or black angular leaf spots surrounded by a faint yellow halo, leading to early defoliation.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment_organic: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + hydrated lime) or copper oxychloride after leaf emergence.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment_chemical: Mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or folpet applied at regular intervals during humid periods.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Maintain proper vineyard weed control and canopy trellis training to facilitate quick drying.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Lush, supple green leaves with clean veination and robust tendril formation. Fruit clusters develop evenly.
Grape___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Maintain vine training and soil health.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Ensure good trellis airflow, balanced potassium and magnesium nutrition, and regular canopy management.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) vectored by Asian Citrus Psyllid
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottling on leaves, yellowing veins, dieback of twigs, small lopsided bitter fruit that stays green at the blossom end.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment_organic: Control the Asian Citrus Psyllid vector using release of parasitic wasps (Tamarixia radiata) and kaolin clay barrier sprays.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment_chemical: Systemic and contact insecticides (imidacloprid, bifenthrin) targeted at psyllid flush cycles. Foliar micronutrient cocktails.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant only certified disease-free rootstock from enclosed insect-proof nurseries. Eradicate confirmed infected trees promptly to prevent spread.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Angular, water-soaked purple-black leaf spots that fall out giving a 'shot-hole' look. Deep cracks and gummy pits on fruit.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment_organic: Apply low-rate fixed copper bactericides or oxytetracycline formulations beginning at shuck split.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment_chemical: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) sprays applied at 7-day intervals from petal fall to shuck split.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant tolerant peach cultivars (e.g., Redhaven, Bountiful). Avoid planting in wind-blown sandy soils without windbreaks.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Long, lance-shaped leaves are vibrant green, pliable, and show zero bacterial pitting or leaf yellowing.
Peach___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Mulch base with organic compost.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Annual thinning, winter pruning for sun access, and careful drip irrigation.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked dark lesions on leaves that become brown and necrotic with yellow haloes. Heavy leaf drop exposes fruit to sunscald.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment_organic: Apply copper hydroxide combined with Bacillus subtilis or Serenade biofungicide. Strip infected lower leaves.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment_chemical: Copper-based bactericides combined with mancozeb to overcome copper-resistant bacterial strains.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds or hot-water treated seeds. Never work in pepper patches while leaves are wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy deep green leaves with crisp edges, strong upright stem stems, and abundant bloom formation.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Maintain balanced compost feed.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Mulch soil with straw or black plastic, irrigate at root level, and rotate with non-solanaceous crops.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Distinctive concentric target-ring brown to black spots on mature lower leaves. Surrounding leaf tissue yellows and wilts.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment_organic: Apply copper octanoate or copper sulfate at first symptom appearance. Prune dead or heavily spotted lower foliage.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment_chemical: Spray chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin on 7 to 10 day cycles when conditions favor fungal sporulation.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium soil levels. Ensure 3-year crop rotation without tomatoes, eggplants, or peppers.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked pale green or dark brown lesions rapidly expanding. White fuzzy spore growth on leaf undersides in humid mornings.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment_organic: Immediate application of copper hydroxide or fixed copper. In severe outbreaks, destroy and bag infected foliage immediately.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment_chemical: Systemic fungicides such as cymoxanil, dimethomorph, mandipropamid, or mefenoxam.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers. Hill soil around potatoes to protect developing tubers from washing spores.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Compound leaves are lush green, robust, and crisp with vigorous bushy upright vine architecture.
Potato___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment needed. Keep rows weeded and hilled.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Regular drip watering, sufficient hilling, and crop rotation.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Bright emerald green pinnate leaves with serrated margins, healthy canes, and vigorous primocane emergence.
Raspberry___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Maintain acidic mulch and pine needles.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out old floricanes after fruiting and maintain 3-foot wide row trellis spacing.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves have uniform medium to dark green color, clear veins, and abundant healthy nodulation at root base.
Soybean___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Inoculate with Rhizobium bacteria at planting.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Practice 2-year corn-soybean rotation and certified weed management.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum-like powdery white spots on leaf blades and petioles. Leaves eventually turn yellow, brown, and dry like paper.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment_organic: Dilute milk spray (40% milk / 60% water), potassium bicarbonate, or neem oil applied every 5 to 7 days.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment_chemical: Apply myclobutanil, quinoxyfen, or cyflufenamid early before mildew covers more than 5% of foliage.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Choose powdery mildew resistant squash varieties. Plant in full sun with wide spacing for maximum air movement.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, dark purple or reddish spots without light centers. As spots multiply, leaves scorch, brown, and curl upward.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment_organic: Apply copper-based fungicides before blossoming. Remove and discard heavily spotted old leaves after renovation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment_chemical: Captan or thiophanate-methyl sprays applied during early leaf flush and post-harvest renovation periods.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Plant in well-drained raised beds with adequate spacing. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation during late afternoon.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Deep emerald, glossy trifoliate leaves with vibrant margins, vigorous runners, and clean white blooms.
Strawberry___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Refresh straw bedding beneath runners.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Clean straw mulch to prevent soil splashing, renovative pruning, and trickle drip lines.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark brown or black angular leaf spots surrounded by a yellow halo. Fruit has small raised scab-like spots.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment_organic: Copper soap spray mixed with Bacillus subtilis. Remove lowest infected leaves touching the soil.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment_chemical: Copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb to manage copper-tolerant bacterial populations.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Never work in garden when plants are wet. Stake and prune tomatoes for airflow. Use seed treated with hot water.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown to black spots on older bottom leaves featuring dark concentric rings resembling a target board. Foliage yellows and dies.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment_organic: Copper-based fungicides, bio-fungicides with Trichoderma. Remove and destroy infected bottom foliage immediately.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment_chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin sprays applied on 7-10 day schedule starting after planting.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch generously to prevent fungal spores in soil from splashing onto lower leaves. Prune lower branches 12 inches off soil.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly spreading irregular water-soaked greasy olive-brown lesions on leaves and stems. White moldy spore growth under moist conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment_organic: Preventive copper fungicides. Infected vines should be immediately pulled, bagged, and disposed of to prevent neighborhood epidemics.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment_chemical: Protectant fungicides containing chlorothalonil, cymoxanil, mandipropamid, or cyazofamid applied aggressively before wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Select late-blight resistant tomato cultivars (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant, Jasper). Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces corresponding to velvety olive-green to brownish fungal patches underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment_organic: Apply sulfur or copper formulations. Greatly reduce relative humidity below 85% by increasing greenhouse ventilation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment_chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, thiophanate-methyl, or triflumizole when first spots appear on lower canopy foliage.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Space greenhouse plants widely. Use exhaust fans and drip irrigation to maintain leaf dryness.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous circular tiny spots (1/8 inch) with grayish-white centers and dark brown borders with tiny black specks in centers.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment_organic: Apply copper octanoate or copper sulfate at 7-day intervals. Prune lower infected leaves up to first flower cluster.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment_chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb applied as protective barrier sprays early in the growing season.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Heavy organic mulch layer under plants. Clean stakes and cages with bleach solution before each planting season.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on leaves accompanied by silky webbing on undersides of leaves. Leaves dry out and turn papery.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment_organic: Insecticidal soap, neem oil, or rosemary-based horticultural oil. Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment_chemical: Abamectin, bifenazate, or spiromesifen miticides applied thoroughly under leaves where mites colonize.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Mist plants periodically in dry dusty spells to increase humidity. Keep garden beds weed-free to eliminate alternate weed hosts.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small pinpoint brown lesions expanding into circular brown spots with faint concentric rings and light brown centers.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment_organic: Copper-based sprays or bio-fungicide formulations. Prune overcrowded suckers and lower branches.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment_chemical: Boscalid, pyraclostrobin, or fludioxonil fungicides applied according to local weather advisories.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Increase row spacing to promote quick canopy drying. Rotate with corn or small grains.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, erect bushy growth, leaves curl upward into cups, mottled yellow margins, and complete flower drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment_organic: Control whitefly vectors using yellow sticky cards, neem oil, and pyrethrin sprays. Roguing (destroying) infected plants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment_chemical: Systemic neonicotinoids or pyrethroids targeted at whitefly nymphs and adults in seedling stage.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids. Use 50-mesh fine insect exclusion netting on greenhouses and nursery beds.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, fern-leaf narrowing/distortion, blistering, and stunted plant vigor.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment_organic: No chemical cure exists once infected. Remove and burn or bag infected plants. Wash hands with milk or trisodium phosphate.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment_chemical: No viral chemicals exist. Control aphids and mechanical spread.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Plant virus-resistant certified varieties (labeled 'T' or 'ToMV'). Prohibit tobacco use near plants (virus travels on smokers' fingers).

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is vibrant emerald green, bushy, robust, and shows clean veins without chlorosis, spots, curling, or webbing.
Tomato___healthy.treatment_organic: No treatment required. Feed with balanced organic tomato fertilizer and calcium to prevent blossom end rot.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Keep plants staked, prune suckers for air movement, mulch the soil line, and water uniformly at ground level.
